writeup.headline: Ouster rates Hold: very fast growth and net cash offset by heavy losses and a high valuation.
writeup.thesis: Ouster scores 48, a Hold, just 4 points above the Sell line. Growth is the standout (score 96), with TTM revenue growth of 62.8% and growth sped up by 7.0 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet also helps (score 80): there is no debt and net cash covers 3.2 years of cash at the current burn. Those strengths are largely cancelled by weak quality (score 15), with an operating margin of -30.6%, an FCF margin of -40.2%, stock-based pay at 18.5% of revenue and diluted share count up 21.2% year on year. Valuation scores just 6: P/S of 11.8 is high in absolute terms, the FCF yield is 8.4 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock is expensive against its own history (P/S more expensive than at 48 of the last 57 month-ends).
key_risks: Continued cash burn and losses, with an FCF margin of -40.2%, could require more capital.
Ongoing dilution, with diluted share count up 21.2% year on year and stock-based pay at 18.5% of revenue.
A high absolute valuation (P/S of 11.8) leaves little room if growth slows.
Competition and pricing pressure from Hesai and other lidar makers.
A volatile share price, now 46.2% below its 52-week high and 7.2% below its 50-day average.
what_would_change: A drop of 4 or more points in the score, for example from weaker trend or news scores or slowing growth, would move the rating to Sell.
Reaching Buy needs 17 more points, which would likely take clear margin and cash-flow improvement lifting the quality score from 15.
A Q3 report on Nov 3 well outside the $54.5M–$57.5M revenue outlook could shift the growth and news scores.
A lower valuation, through a price decline or fast revenue growth that shrinks P/S, would lift the valuation score from 6.
